sections.title: Rendering the markdown
sections.explanation: Builds markdown tables for the latest row, the indicators and recent closes, stating both the requested date and the latest row used. The closing paragraph instructs the model to flag conflicts rather than reconcile them and not to claim validated bounces without concrete evidence.

tradingagents/agents/managers/research_m.overview: Factory for the Research Manager node from Step 11. It judges the bull/bear debate and produces a structured ResearchPlan with a five-tier rating (Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell), which becomes the `investment_plan` the Trader reads. It uses the structured-output helpers with a free-text fallback.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports the instrument context and language helpers, the ResearchPlan schema and its renderer, and the structured-output utilities including the NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS prompt fragment.

sections.title: Factory and state reads
sections.explanation: Binds the LLM to ResearchPlan once at construction time. The node reads the full debate history from `investment_debate_state`.

sections.title: Judging prompt
sections.explanation: Defines the rating scale and, notably, tells the model that conflict alone is not a reason to Hold: it must commit to the stronger side, sized by how decisively it wins, and choose Hold only when evidence is genuinely balanced or thin. It also asks the model to ignore speaking order.

sections.title: Invoke and update state
sections.explanation: Produces the plan through `invoke_structured_or_freetext`, then writes a new debate state that preserves the histories and count but sets `current_response` to the plan, and stores the plan as `investment_plan` for the Trader.

tradingagents/agents/researchers/bear_re.overview: Factory for the Bear Researcher node in the Step 11 debate. It reads the four analyst reports and the debate so far, then argues the case against the instrument and rebuts the latest bull argument. Each turn appends to the shared and bear-specific histories and increments the count that the routing logic uses to end the debate.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Pulls helpers from agents.context: `opponent_argument_or_opening` handles the first round when there is no bull argument yet, and `report_or_absent` substitutes a clear placeholder for a missing analyst report.

sections.title: Gathering debate inputs
sections.explanation: Reads the histories and the last bull argument, the four analyst reports, and the asset type. Labels adapt for non-stock assets, noting that fundamentals may be unavailable for crypto.

sections.title: Bear prompt
sections.explanation: A plain-text prompt (no structured output) asking for risks, competitive weaknesses and negative indicators, and for direct engagement with the bull's points in a conversational style. All resources are inlined into the prompt.

sections.title: Invoke and update debate state
sections.explanation: Prefixes the response with 'Bear Analyst:', appends it to `history` and `bear_history`, sets it as `current_response` for the bull's next turn, and increments `count`, which the conditional routing uses to stop after the configured number of rounds.

tradingagents/agents/researchers/bull_re.overview: Defines the Bull Researcher node, one of the two voices in the investment debate. It reads the four analyst reports and the running debate, asks the LLM for a pro-investment argument that rebuts the bear, and appends that argument to the shared `investment_debate_state`. The routing in Step 7's conditional logic alternates this node with the Bear Researcher until the round limit is reached.

sections.title: Context helper imports
sections.explanation: Imports small helpers from `agents/context.py`. `report_or_absent` replaces an empty analyst report with an explicit 'absent' note, and `opponent_argument_or_opening` does the same for the opponent's last turn, so the prompt never contains a blank that the model might fill in with invented content.

sections.title: Gathering debate inputs
sections.explanation: `create_bull_researcher` is a factory: it closes over `llm` and returns the node function LangGraph calls. The node pulls the full history, its own history and the bear's latest response out of the debate sub-state, then normalizes each analyst report. `asset_type` switches the wording between 'stock' and 'asset', and warns that fundamentals may be unavailable for crypto.

sections.title: The bull prompt
sections.explanation: A single f-string prompt lists the bull's focus areas (growth, competitive advantages, positive indicators, rebuttal of bear points) and injects every resource plus the debate history. `get_language_instruction()` is appended so output language follows the configured setting. The prompt explicitly asks for a conversational debate style rather than a data dump.

sections.title: Updating the debate state
sections.explanation: The response is prefixed with 'Bull Analyst:' and appended to both the shared `history` and `bull_history`, while `bear_history` is passed through untouched. `current_response` becomes this argument so the bear sees it next, and `count` is incremented; the conditional logic compares this counter against the configured round limit to decide when to hand off to the Research Manager.

tradingagents/agents/structured.py.overview: Shared helpers that implement the structured-output-with-fallback pattern used by the Research Manager, Trader and Portfolio Manager. At agent creation the LLM is bound to a Pydantic schema from Step 5; at invocation the structured call runs, and any failure degrades to a plain free-text call so the pipeline never stalls. Centralizing this keeps the agent factories small and the warning messages consistent.

sections.title: Module docstring: the pattern
sections.explanation: The docstring documents the two-stage contract: bind with `with_structured_output(Schema)` once (skip if unsupported), then at each call try structured and fall back to `llm.invoke` on any error. Reading this first explains why the three decision agents look so similar.

sections.title: Imports and NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS
sections.explanation: `T` is a TypeVar bound to `BaseModel`, letting the helpers stay generic over any schema. `NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS` is a prompt sentence agents append because schema-only structured output binds exactly one tool; if the model tries to call a search tool instead, the structured attempt is wasted and retried as free text.

sections.title: bind_structured
sections.explanation: Wraps `llm.with_structured_output(schema)` and returns `None` when the provider raises `NotImplementedError` or `AttributeError`. Returning `None` instead of raising lets the agent keep working in free-text mode for every call, and the warning tells the user this is a permanent mode, not a one-off fallback.

sections.title: invoke_structured
sections.explanation: Runs the structured call and returns the parsed model or `None`. A `None` result from the parser (a thinking model that answered in prose instead of calling the tool) is converted into an error so it follows the same fallback path. Catching broad `Exception` is deliberate: malformed JSON or a transient provider error should not abort the graph.

sections.title: invoke_structured_or_freetext
sections.explanation: The convenience wrapper most agents use: on success it renders the Pydantic result to markdown via the supplied `render` function; otherwise it calls the plain LLM with the same prompt and returns `.content`. Because `prompt` is passed through unchanged, callers can use either a string or a list of message dicts.

tradingagents/agents/trader/trader.py.overview: Defines the Trader node, which converts the Research Manager's investment plan into a concrete TraderProposal with action, reasoning and price levels. It grounds price levels in the technical market report when one exists, includes the caller's portfolio context, and uses the structured-output helpers so the result is typed when possible and free text otherwise. Its output feeds the risk debate in Step 12.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Pulls in context helpers (instrument, portfolio, language), the `TraderProposal` schema and its markdown renderer, and the structured-output helpers from `structured.py`. `AIMessage` is used to append the plan to the graph's message channel.

sections.title: Factory and input gathering
sections.explanation: `bind_structured` runs once when the node is created, not on every call. The node reads the investment plan and the market report; the comment explains (#1167) that the research plan loses exact price structure, so the technical report is supplied for entry and stop levels. When the market analyst was not selected the report is empty, so both the report section and the grounding instruction are omitted.

sections.title: System and user messages
sections.explanation: The prompt is a list of role/content dicts. The system message insists entry and stop-loss be absolute prices, never percentages or ranges, because a value like '15%' fails the numeric field in the structured parse (#1288). The user message carries the plan and context, and specifies output sections, including the rule that Overweight maps to Buy and Underweight to Sell, so conflict alone does not produce a Hold.

sections.title: Invocation and state update
sections.explanation: `invoke_structured_or_freetext` returns markdown either way, so the rest of the graph sees a uniform string. The node writes it to `trader_investment_plan`, which the risk debaters and Portfolio Manager read, and also appends it to `messages` as an `AIMessage`.

tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_.overview: Defines the Portfolio Manager, the last node of the graph. It reads the risk debate, the research plan, the trader's proposal, the caller's portfolio and lessons from past settled decisions, then produces a typed PortfolioDecision whose rating becomes the run's `final_rating`. Unlike the Trader, it keeps the typed rating separate from the rendered text so a rating quoted inside the thesis can never override the actual decision.

sections.title: Docstring and imports
sections.explanation: The docstring states the contract: one structured call producing `PortfolioDecision`, rendered to markdown as `final_trade_decision` for the memory log, CLI and reports. It imports `parse_rating` for the free-text fallback and only `invoke_structured` (not the or-freetext wrapper), because this node needs the typed object itself.

sections.title: Gathering context and lessons
sections.explanation: The schema binding happens once at creation. The node collects instrument and portfolio context, the risk debate history, the research plan and trader plan. `past_context` is injected by the orchestrator from the memory log (Step 13); the lessons line is only added when it is non-empty, so a first run does not show an empty heading.

sections.title: Decision prompt
sections.explanation: The prompt defines the five-tier rating scale and stresses that conflict in the risk debate is expected and is not by itself a reason to Hold; Hold is reserved for balanced or thin evidence. It also asks the model to weigh analysts on merit regardless of speaking order, and closes with `NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS` and the language instruction.

sections.title: Typed rating vs text fallback
sections.explanation: On structured success the rating comes straight from `decision.rating.value`; only on fallback is it parsed from free text with `parse_rating`, which returns REVIEW rather than defaulting to Hold. The comment spells out why: reading the rating back from rendered text could pick up a rating mentioned inside the thesis.

sections.title: Closing the risk debate
sections.explanation: The node rebuilds `risk_debate_state` with all histories preserved and `latest_speaker` set to 'Judge', marking the debate as concluded. It returns that state plus `final_trade_decision` and `final_rating`, the two values the orchestrator stores in the memory log.

tradingagents/agents/risk_mgmt/aggressiv.overview: Defines the Aggressive Risk Analyst node, one of three voices in the risk debate that challenges the trader's proposal. This debater champions high-reward, high-risk opportunities and argues for the trader's plan on its upside. It reads the trader's plan, the analyst reports and the caller's portfolio, responds to the conservative and neutral analysts' latest arguments, and appends its turn to `risk_debate_state` for the Portfolio Manager to judge.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Uses the same context helpers as the research debaters, plus `get_portfolio_context_from_state`, because risk arguments depend on what the caller already holds.

sections.title: Reading the debate and reports
sections.explanation: The factory closes over `llm` and returns the node. The node reads the shared history and its own history, then fetches the latest responses of the conservative and neutral analysts through `opponent_argument_or_opening`, which marks a missing turn explicitly (useful when this node speaks first). Reports are normalized with `report_or_absent`, and the trader's plan is read from `trader_investment_plan`.

sections.title: The aggressive prompt
sections.explanation: A single f-string sets the Aggressive persona, embeds the trader's decision, the instrument and portfolio context and all four reports, and asks the model to rebut the conservative and neutral analysts point by point. It asks for conversational output without special formatting, since these turns are concatenated into a transcript, and appends the language instruction.

sections.title: Updating risk debate state
sections.explanation: The response is prefixed with 'Aggressive Analyst:' and appended to `history` and `aggressive_history`; the other histories and current responses are passed through unchanged. `latest_speaker` is set to 'Aggressive', which the conditional logic from Step 7 uses to pick the next speaker, and `count` is incremented toward the round limit.

tradingagents/agents/risk_mgmt/conservat.overview: Defines the Conservative Risk Analyst node, one of three voices in the risk debate that challenges the trader's proposal. This debater prioritizes protecting capital and argues for lower-risk adjustments to the trader's plan. It reads the trader's plan, the analyst reports and the caller's portfolio, responds to the aggressive and neutral analysts' latest arguments, and appends its turn to `risk_debate_state` for the Portfolio Manager to judge.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Uses the same context helpers as the research debaters, plus `get_portfolio_context_from_state`, because risk arguments depend on what the caller already holds.

sections.title: Reading the debate and reports
sections.explanation: The factory closes over `llm` and returns the node. The node reads the shared history and its own history, then fetches the latest responses of the aggressive and neutral analysts through `opponent_argument_or_opening`, which marks a missing turn explicitly (useful when this node speaks first). Reports are normalized with `report_or_absent`, and the trader's plan is read from `trader_investment_plan`.

sections.title: The conservative prompt
sections.explanation: A single f-string sets the Conservative persona, embeds the trader's decision, the instrument and portfolio context and all four reports, and asks the model to rebut the aggressive and neutral analysts point by point. It asks for conversational output without special formatting, since these turns are concatenated into a transcript, and appends the language instruction.

sections.title: Updating risk debate state
sections.explanation: The response is prefixed with 'Conservative Analyst:' and appended to `history` and `conservative_history`; the other histories and current responses are passed through unchanged. `latest_speaker` is set to 'Conservative', which the conditional logic from Step 7 uses to pick the next speaker, and `count` is incremented toward the round limit.

tradingagents/agents/risk_mgmt/neutral_d.overview: Defines the Neutral Risk Analyst node, one of three voices in the risk debate that challenges the trader's proposal. This debater weighs upside and downside and argues for a balanced, moderate adjustment. It reads the trader's plan, the analyst reports and the caller's portfolio, responds to the aggressive and conservative analysts' latest arguments, and appends its turn to `risk_debate_state` for the Portfolio Manager to judge.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Uses the same context helpers as the research debaters, plus `get_portfolio_context_from_state`, because risk arguments depend on what the caller already holds.

sections.title: Reading the debate and reports
sections.explanation: The factory closes over `llm` and returns the node. The node reads the shared history and its own history, then fetches the latest responses of the aggressive and conservative analysts through `opponent_argument_or_opening`, which marks a missing turn explicitly (useful when this node speaks first). Reports are normalized with `report_or_absent`, and the trader's plan is read from `trader_investment_plan`.

sections.title: The neutral prompt
sections.explanation: A single f-string sets the Neutral persona, embeds the trader's decision, the instrument and portfolio context and all four reports, and asks the model to rebut the aggressive and conservative analysts point by point. It asks for conversational output without special formatting, since these turns are concatenated into a transcript, and appends the language instruction.

sections.title: Updating risk debate state
sections.explanation: The response is prefixed with 'Neutral Analyst:' and appended to `history` and `neutral_history`; the other histories and current responses are passed through unchanged. `latest_speaker` is set to 'Neutral', which the conditional logic from Step 7 uses to pick the next speaker, and `count` is incremented toward the round limit.

tradingagents/portfolio.py.overview: Models the caller's portfolio (positions, cash, currency) as optional input to a run, and renders it as a text block for the Trader, risk debaters and Portfolio Manager. The docstring stresses three distinct states, a held position, a flat book and no context at all, because treating 'not provided' as 'flat' would invent a fact about the caller's account. It is broker-neutral: quantities are generic units and currency is just a label.

sections.title: Docstring and imports
sections.explanation: Explains the purpose and the three-state rule, then imports Pydantic for validation and `normalize_symbol` so holdings can be matched across broker spellings of the same instrument.

sections.title: Position model
sections.explanation: A Pydantic model for one holding. `allow_inf_nan=False` rejects infinite or NaN numbers at validation time. `quantity` is signed so a short position is negative, and `average_price` is optional.

sections.title: PortfolioContext and lookups
sections.explanation: The container model: optional cash and currency plus a list of positions. `positions_in` normalizes both the requested ticker and each holding's ticker so BTCUSDT or 700.HK spellings match the analyzed instrument, while holdings keep their original spelling. `position_in` returns the first match or `None`.

sections.title: render for the agents
sections.explanation: Builds the 'Portfolio at the analysis date' block, leading with the analyzed instrument. It notes the original spelling when it differs ('listed as ...'), states 'No current position' explicitly for a flat book, adds cash when given, and summarizes other positions. Identity comparison (`is not`) is used to exclude already-listed holdings.

sections.title: fingerprint
sections.explanation: A short SHA-256 digest of the serialized model. It lets checkpointing detect that the book changed, so a resumed run cannot continue with stale portfolio assumptions.

sections.title: load_portfolio
sections.explanation: Reads and validates a JSON file, converting file, JSON and validation errors into a single `ValueError`. The goal, per the docstring, is to fail before the graph starts rather than mid-run.

tradingagents/backtest.py.overview: Runs the TradingAgentsGraph over a grid of tickers and dates and scores the results by rating. It reuses the memory log as its results table: every run already records its rating and later settles it with raw and alpha returns, so the backtest just isolates a log per run and aggregates it. The docstring is explicit that this evaluates decision quality and is not a portfolio simulator.

sections.title: Scope and imports
sections.explanation: The module docstring sets the boundaries: cells are independent, no quantities, fills or cash ledger are modeled, and a supplied portfolio is the same standing book for every cell. Imports bring in the graph, the memory log, the REVIEW rating sentinel and date and path-safety helpers.

sections.title: Building the date grid
sections.explanation: `iter_grid` produces dates every `every_n_days`, capped at today because a future date has nothing to settle against and the graph rejects it. `_canonical` parses strictly and round-trips the string, so a date like '2024-1-5' is rejected even though `strptime` would accept it.

sections.title: Result and score types
sections.explanation: `_alpha` converts the log's percentage string back to a fraction, accurate to 0.1 percentage point. `_DIRECTION` maps each rating to the direction it claims; Hold claims none, so it gets no hit rate. `BacktestSummary.render` prints per-rating counts, hit rates and mean alpha, and adds a caveat that results are indicative because model sampling and text feeds are not reproducible.

sections.title: Claiming a run directory
sections.explanation: `_new_run` creates a timestamped directory using `mkdir()` without `exist_ok`, so the filesystem acts as an atomic claim: if another sweep took the same second, a numeric suffix is tried next.

sections.title: run_backtest: setup and resume
sections.explanation: Each run gets its own `results_dir` and `memory_log_path`, so the live log real runs read for lessons is not flooded. A user-supplied `run_id` is validated with `safe_ticker_component` because it becomes a path segment. Cells already in the run's log are skipped, which is how an interrupted sweep resumes, and `dict.fromkeys` dedupes tickers and dates while preserving order.

sections.title: run_backtest: cells and settlement
sections.explanation: Each cell calls `graph.propagate`; exceptions are recorded instead of ending the sweep. Afterwards a settlement pass runs per ticker, because normally settlement happens at the start of the next run for that ticker, which would leave each ticker's last cell pending. Settlement and reflection failures are collected separately.

sections.title: summarize
sections.explanation: Loads entries from a result or a log path and keeps only settled entries with a readable rating and alpha. For each rating it computes the count, a hit rate (the share of cells where alpha has the claimed sign) and mean alpha. REVIEW entries are counted as unscored, and the holding window is read from the log itself so the report states what was actually measured.

tradingagents/memory/log.py.overview: Implements TradingMemoryLog, an append-only Markdown file that records each decision with its rating and, once settled, its returns and a reflection. Runs write a pending entry at the end of propagation; settlement later rewrites the entry's tag and appends a REFLECTION section; the Portfolio Manager reads formatted past context back from it. File locks and atomic replace keep it safe across concurrent runs.

sections.title: Format constants and init
sections.explanation: Entries are separated by an HTML comment, `<!-- ENTRY_END -->`, chosen because it will not appear in LLM prose. Regexes for the DECISION and REFLECTION sections are precompiled once at class level. The constructor resolves and creates the log's directory, and reads an optional `memory_log_max_entries` cap for rotation.

sections.title: store_decision
sections.explanation: Appends a pending entry tagged `[date | ticker | rating | pending]`. Under a file lock it first scans raw lines for any entry with the same date and ticker, pending or settled, and returns early; otherwise a re-run would count the same decision twice. The rating comes from the caller's typed value when available, else from `parse_rating`.

sections.title: settling lock
sections.explanation: Returns a separate lock (`<log>.settle`) held for an entire settlement pass, so two processes do not pay for the same LLM reflections. With no log path it returns a `nullcontext(True)`, and `wait=False` lets a caller skip if another pass is already running.

sections.title: Reading entries
sections.explanation: `load_entries` splits the file on the separator and parses each block, dropping malformed ones. `get_pending_entries` filters for entries still awaiting an outcome, which is what settlement iterates over.

sections.title: get_past_context
sections.explanation: Builds the lessons text injected into the Portfolio Manager prompt: up to `n_same` full entries for the same ticker and `n_cross` reflection-only entries for other tickers, newest first. When `as_of` is given, only entries resolved on or before that date are used, so a historical or backtest run cannot learn from outcomes that had not happened yet (#1251).

sections.title: update_with_outcome
sections.explanation: Under the write lock, finds the first pending block for the ticker and date, replaces its tag with the resolved tag (returns, holding days, optional resolution date) and appends the reflection. It writes to a `.tmp` file and uses `replace` so a crash cannot leave a half-written log. It returns `False` if no pending entry was found, for example when another pass settled it first.

sections.title: batch_update_with_outcomes
sections.explanation: The same rewrite for many updates in one read and one atomic write. A dict keyed by (date, ticker) is consumed as blocks match, so each update applies to at most one block.

sections.title: Tags and rotation
sections.explanation: `_resolved_tag` builds the six-field tag and adds `resolved:YYYY-MM-DD` when known, keeping older logs compatible. `_apply_rotation` drops the oldest resolved blocks when the cap is exceeded, ordering by decision date then position, and never drops pending blocks since they are unfinished work.

sections.title: Parsing and formatting
sections.explanation: `_parse_entry` splits the tag on '|' into date, ticker, rating, pending flag, raw, alpha, holding and the optional resolved date, then extracts the decision and reflection with the regexes. `_format_full` and `_format_reflection_only` render entries for prompts; the latter falls back to the first 300 characters of the decision when no reflection exists.

tradingagents/memory/reflection.py.overview: Defines the Reflector, which asks the quick-thinking LLM to turn a settled decision's outcome into a short lesson. Settlement calls it once per settled entry, the lesson is stored in the memory log's REFLECTION section, and later runs feed it to the Portfolio Manager as past context.

sections.title: Reflector and system prompt
sections.explanation: The Reflector just holds the LLM. `_system_prompt` asks for 2-4 sentences of plain prose, compact enough to re-inject into later prompts. It names the holding window explicitly, because a thesis written for months is not disproved by a week, and asks the model to say so when the window is too short to judge.

sections.title: reflect_on_final_decision
sections.explanation: Builds a system and human message pair as tuples, with raw return and alpha against the named benchmark formatted as signed percentages, plus the final decision text. No separate market context is passed because the final decision already synthesizes the analyst insights. It returns the model's `.content` string.

tradingagents/memory/settlement.py.overview: Settles past decisions once their holding window has traded: it picks a regional benchmark, fetches final closes for the instrument and the benchmark, computes raw and alpha returns, asks the Reflector for a lesson and writes the outcome into the memory log. It is careful never to settle on partial windows or live intraday prices, and records the resolution date for point-in-time filtering.

sections.title: Imports and resolve_benchmark
sections.explanation: `resolve_benchmark` uses an explicit `benchmark_ticker` from config when set (normalized like any symbol, otherwise it would find no prices), else matches the ticker's exchange suffix against `benchmark_map`, falling back to the empty-suffix entry or SPY. Tickers with dots like BRK.B fall through to the default.

sections.title: Clock and daily bars
sections.explanation: `_now` is isolated so tests can patch it. `_by_day` drops non-positive closes, keys bars by calendar day so series from different time zones align on dates, and removes today's bar in the market's own time zone because that close is still the live price.

sections.title: fetch_returns: windows
sections.explanation: Entry is the first close after the trade date, since a run dated that day reads news published after the close (#1518). The function returns all `None` early if not enough calendar days have passed. It requests a calendar span of about 7 days per 5 trading days plus a week of slack, starts the benchmark a week early, and widens the request through today if a long closure kept the window from trading.

sections.title: fetch_returns: computing alpha
sections.explanation: It requires the full holding window to have traded, otherwise the entry stays pending (#1169). The benchmark must cover entry through exit; it is valued with `asof` at each end so both returns span the same dates even when calendars differ, such as a coin that trades on weekends. The exit bar's date becomes `resolution_date`.

sections.title: Settlement result
sections.explanation: A small dataclass listing settled (ticker, date) pairs and failures with reasons, so callers like the backtest can report what happened.

sections.title: settle_pending
sections.explanation: Holds the log's settling lock, then for each pending entry of the ticker fetches returns, asks for a reflection and writes the outcome immediately, so an interrupted pass keeps its finished work. Price or reflection errors are logged and recorded while the entry stays pending; a window that has not traded is silently skipped.

sections.title: settle_all_pending
sections.explanation: Runs `settle_pending` for every ticker with pending entries (#1445). Without this, a ticker that is no longer analyzed would keep its decisions pending forever and its lessons would never reach later runs.

cli/display.py.overview: Owns the Rich-based live terminal view of a run: a module-level `MessageBuffer` that accumulates messages, tool calls, agent statuses and report sections, plus the functions that render them into a header/progress/messages/report/footer layout. `cli/run.py` feeds streamed graph chunks into these helpers, which is the heart of tour step 14's interactive CLI. It also tracks per-analyst wall time for the parallel analyst team.

sections.title: Imports and shared console
sections.explanation: Imports Rich layout primitives and the analyst execution specs from `tradingagents.graph.analyst_execution`. A single module-level `console = Console()` is shared by the whole CLI (`cli/main.py`, `cli/run.py`, `cli/selections.py` all import it), so output styling stays consistent.

sections.title: MessageBuffer state model
sections.explanation: `MessageBuffer` declares the fixed teams that always run, the analyst key-to-display-name mapping (note the sentiment analyst's key is `social`), and `REPORT_SECTIONS`, which pairs each state field with the analyst that gates it and the agent whose completion finalizes it. `init_for_analysis` resets statuses and report slots for only the selected analysts. `get_completed_reports_count` counts a report as done only when it has content *and* its finalizing agent is completed, so interim debate rounds do not inflate the footer counter.

sections.title: Mutators and current report
sections.explanation: Small mutators append timestamped messages and tool calls to bounded `deque`s (max 100) and update statuses only for agents that are tracked. `_update_current_report` picks the last non-empty section in dict order and formats it with a human title for the 'Current Report' panel. A single global `message_buffer` instance is created at import time, which `cli/run.py` monkey-patches to also log to disk.

sections.title: Layout and token formatting
sections.explanation: `create_layout` splits the screen into header, main (progress + messages over a large analysis panel) and footer using ratios. `format_tokens` renders counts like `12.3k` for the stats footer.

sections.title: update_display renderer
sections.explanation: Rebuilds every panel from the global buffer on each call: a progress table grouped by team with spinners for in-progress agents, a messages table merging tool calls and messages sorted newest-first (truncated to 200 chars and 12 rows), the current report as Markdown, and a footer with agent/report counts, LLM/tool/token stats from the callback handler and elapsed time. Sorting by `HH:MM:SS` strings works within a single day's run.

sections.title: Final full report printout
sections.explanation: `display_complete_report` prints the whole final state sequentially as panels in the five-part order (analysts, research, trader, risk, portfolio manager). Printing outside the live view avoids the truncation the fixed-size layout would impose.

sections.title: Status transition helpers
sections.explanation: `update_research_team_status` flips all three research agents at once. `update_analyst_statuses` treats analysts as running in parallel: each stays in progress until its report appears in the accumulated sections (not just the current chunk), and once all selected analysts have filed it marks the Bull Researcher in progress, signalling the debate has begun.

sections.title: Message content extraction
sections.explanation: `extract_content_string` normalizes LangChain message content that may be a string, dict, or list of content blocks, keeping only text parts; its `is_empty` helper deliberately judges strings by whitespace so literal text like "0" or "None" is not dropped. `classify_message_type` maps message classes to display types (User/Control/Data/Agent), importing LangChain lazily, and `format_tool_args` truncates argument reprs.

sections.title: Analyst wall-time tracking
sections.explanation: `AnalystWallTimeTracker` records monotonic start times and durations per analyst key, validating keys against `ANALYST_NODE_SPECS` and using `setdefault`/early returns so repeated calls are idempotent. `sync_analyst_tracker_from_chunk` starts every analyst's clock and stops each one when its report key appears in a chunk, and `format_summary` yields the 'Analyst wall time' line shown at the end of a run.

cli/main.py.overview: The Typer entry point behind the `tradingagents` console command. A bare invocation runs an analysis (via `cli.run.run_analysis`), and subcommands provide `backtest`, `login` and `logout`. It translates command-line flags into the `flags` dict and portfolio context the rest of the CLI consumes, and converts setup errors into clean exit codes. This is the front door described in tour step 14.

sections.title: Imports and Windows console guard
sections.explanation: Imports the shared console, CLI models, the run entry point and backtest helpers. The `_NO_CONSOLE_ERRORS` tuple is populated only on Windows because prompt_toolkit's win32 module asserts the platform on import; elsewhere an empty tuple in an `except` clause never matches, so no exception is accidentally swallowed.

sections.title: Typer app definition
sections.explanation: Creates the Typer application with shell completion enabled. The project's console script points at this `app`.

sections.title: analyze: the default command
sections.explanation: Registered with `@app.callback(invoke_without_command=True)` so a bare `tradingagents` runs an analysis, returning early when a subcommand was invoked. Options cover checkpoint resume (tri-state `bool | None` so omission defers to the environment), clearing checkpoints, a portfolio JSON, and flags (`--ticker`, `--date`, `--analysts`, `--save/--show/--html`) that pre-answer interactive prompts. A missing Windows console buffer is reported as a single plain stderr line instead of a traceback.

sections.title: backtest subcommand
sections.explanation: Parses a ticker list and date grid (`iter_grid`), optional portfolio, asset type and analyst choice (defaulting to every analyst the asset type allows), turning any `ValueError` into a red message and exit code 1. It then calls `run_backtest` with a progress callback, prints the `summarize(...)` table, and reports skipped cells, the run id for continuing a sweep, and per-cell or settlement failures.

sections.title: login and logout for signed-in plans
sections.explanation: `Plan` is a `StrEnum` built dynamically from `SIGNED_IN_PROVIDERS`, so the argument choices track whichever providers use sign-in rather than API keys. `login` lazily imports `chatgpt_auth` and prints the sign-in address unwrapped so it can be copied whole; `logout` distinguishes a server-side revoke from a local-only forget and tells the user accordingly.

cli/run.py.overview: Runs one analysis from the CLI: gathers selections, builds the run config, constructs `TradingAgentsGraph`, streams the graph into the live Rich view from `cli/display.py`, and finally offers to save and show the report. It also handles checkpoint resume, per-run message/tool logs, and unattended (no-TTY) runs. This file is where tour step 14's CLI meets the orchestrator from steps 6-7.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Pulls in display helpers and the global `message_buffer`, selection helpers, the stats callback handler, rating helpers, the ticker path sanitizer and the graph classes. The import list itself maps the run lifecycle: select, configure, stream, display, rate.

sections.title: Run directory and resume notice
sections.explanation: `_run_directory` builds `results_dir/<ticker>/<date>` but passes the ticker through `safe_ticker_component` so a value like `..` cannot escape the results directory. `_announce_checkpoint_state` pushes a 'Resuming'/'Starting fresh' message into the buffer because the live view owns the screen and normal logging would be invisible.

sections.title: Building the run config
sections.explanation: Copies `DEFAULT_CONFIG` and applies the interactive choices while honoring 'explicit env/flag wins': a round count set by an environment variable is kept and the user is told the chosen depth does not apply to it. Provider-specific thinking knobs are copied only when set, and `checkpoint_enabled` is overridden only when the flag was explicitly given.

sections.title: Unattended check and graph setup
sections.explanation: With no TTY, `unattended_gaps` lists every flag or variable still missing and exits before any model call. Otherwise it collects selections, orders analysts by `ANALYST_ORDER`, builds the analyst execution plan and wall-time tracker, constructs `TradingAgentsGraph` with the stats callback, and creates the per-run results/reports folders and `message_tool.log`.

sections.title: Logging decorators on the buffer
sections.explanation: Three closures wrap `add_message`, `add_tool_call` and `update_report_section` on the global buffer so every UI update is also appended to the log file or written as a per-section markdown file. Monkey-patching the instance keeps `cli/display.py` free of file I/O.

sections.title: Live view and checkpoint wiring
sections.explanation: Enters a Rich `Live` context on the alternate screen (so a tall layout does not scroll), seeds system messages and marks all analysts in progress since they start together. It builds the initial state with `create_run_state`, gets stream args from the propagator, and calls `begin_checkpoint`; when a thread id comes back it is injected into the LangGraph config so the run can save and resume.

sections.title: Streaming loop and team status
sections.explanation: Iterates `graph.stream_run(...)`, deduplicating messages by id, classifying them for the log and recording tool calls. A `None` chunk is an inner analyst step that only refreshes the display; real chunks update analyst statuses, then the research debate, trader and risk debate sections, flipping agent statuses as judge outputs appear. Each chunk is appended to `trace`.

sections.title: Finalize state and checkpoint cleanup
sections.explanation: Streamed chunks are per-node deltas, so they are merged into `final_state`. On a clean run the decision is recorded in memory and the checkpoint cleared; the `finally` always calls `end_checkpoint` to restore the plain graph even if streaming raised, preserving the checkpoint for resume. Remaining agents are marked completed and report panels refreshed.

sections.title: Post-run messaging
sections.explanation: After leaving the live screen, it warns when no rating could be parsed (`is_review`) so the run is not mistaken for a position, prints the analyst wall-time summary, and hands off to `_offer_reports` with the save/show/html flags.

sections.title: Report saving and browser opening
sections.explanation: `_offer_reports` saves via `graph.save_reports` under the configured results directory (important in Docker, where it is the mounted volume), prompting for path and HTML only when the user answered interactively. `_graphical_browser` refuses SSH sessions and terminal browsers like lynx/elinks, and `_open_page` falls back to printing the page path if opening fails.

cli/selections.py.overview: Collects the settings for a run: ticker, date, output language, analysts, research depth, LLM provider and models, and provider-specific reasoning knobs. Each step can be skipped by a CLI flag or a `TRADINGAGENTS_*` environment variable, and previous answers are remembered as defaults. It also validates that every provider used by the quick and deep model tiers is reachable and authenticated before any paid call. Part of tour step 14's CLI flow.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Imports the shared console, last-run preference helpers, and a large set of prompt/parse helpers from `cli.prompts`, plus config and provider utilities. Keeping prompt widgets in `cli.prompts` lets this module focus on step ordering and precedence rules.

sections.title: Public entry and env helpers
sections.explanation: `get_user_selections` loads the last run's answers, walks the prompts and saves the result. `depth_from_env` is true only when both round-count variables are set. `unattended_gaps` enumerates every flag or variable a no-terminal run still needs, so `cli/run.py` can report them all at once.

sections.title: Checking tier providers
sections.explanation: For each tier (quick, deep), resolves its provider, requires the tier's model variable when the tier runs on a non-main provider, and validates the endpoint with `check_endpoint`. Sign-in and API keys are then ensured once per provider used, so a missing key for the deep tier fails up front rather than after the analysts have already been paid for.

sections.title: Flag parsing helper
sections.explanation: `_from_flag` runs a flag value through the same parser its prompt uses, converting a `ValueError` into a red message and exit code 1, so flags and prompts share validation.

sections.title: Welcome panel and prompt helpers
sections.explanation: Prints the ASCII welcome banner from `static/welcome.txt` in a Rich panel and shows update notices (refreshed in the background, never blocking). The nested `create_question_box` styles each step, and `thinking_value_or_prompt` returns the env-configured value when its variable is set, otherwise prompts.

sections.title: Steps 1-5: ticker to depth
sections.explanation: Ticker, date and analysts honor flags first, falling back to prompts; the asset type is detected from the ticker and announced only when it is not a stock. Output language and research depth are skipped when their environment variables are set. Preferences are sanitized for the asset type before offering remembered analysts.

sections.title: Step 6: provider and endpoint
sections.explanation: Uses the env provider if set, otherwise the menu, with secondary region prompts for qwen, minimax and glm (whose regional accounts cannot share keys). An env backend URL always wins over the menu default, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint is prompted when none is known, and Ollama's endpoint is confirmed. Then `_check_tier_providers` runs.

sections.title: Steps 7-8 and result dict
sections.explanation: Quick/deep models come from the environment or from provider-specific menus (remembered models reused only when the provider is unchanged). Step 8 asks for Gemini thinking level, OpenAI-style reasoning effort or Claude effort depending on the provider, leaving `None` for provider defaults. Everything is returned in one dict that `_build_run_config` consumes.

sections.title: Date prompt loop
sections.explanation: `get_analysis_date` re-prompts until `parse_analysis_date` accepts the input, defaulting to today.

tradingagents/reporting.py.overview: A shared writer that turns a completed run's final state into an on-disk report tree: per-agent markdown files in numbered folders plus a consolidated `complete_report.md` and optional `complete_report.html`. Both the CLI (through `graph.save_reports`) and the programmatic API use it, so headless and interactive runs produce identical output. It is the final step of the CLI flow in tour step 14.

sections.title: Module docstring and imports
sections.explanation: Explains that the CLI and `TradingAgentsGraph.save_reports` both call this writer. It imports `run_rating` to include the parsed rating in the report header.

sections.title: Analyst names and header
sections.explanation: `analyst_names` maps the internal `social` key back to the user-facing 'sentiment'. `_header` builds the report title and provenance bullets: analysis date, rating, generation time and, when run settings are provided, version, models (collapsed when both tiers share a provider, otherwise per tier), analysts, debate rounds and data vendors, plus any memory-log note.

sections.title: Section table
sections.explanation: `_SECTIONS` is a declarative table of (heading, folder, agents), where each agent entry names its output file and a key path into the state (for example `risk_debate_state -> aggressive_history`). Keeping the layout as data lets both the markdown writer and the HTML renderer share one ordering.

sections.title: Collecting report parts
sections.explanation: `_report_parts` walks each key path through the final state, tolerating missing intermediate dicts with `(value or {})`, and keeps only sections that have at least one non-empty entry.

sections.title: Writing the tree and reconciling
sections.explanation: `write_report_tree` writes each agent file and a combined markdown report, then either renders HTML via a lazily imported `report_html.render_report` or deletes a stale HTML file. Finally it removes only the files this writer owns that are absent from this run, never clearing the directory, so user notes kept alongside reports survive reuse of the same folder. It returns the path of `complete_report.md`.

.github/workflows/ci.yml.overview: The main GitHub Actions CI pipeline, run on pushes to `main` and version branches and on every pull request. It runs the test suite across Python 3.11-3.14 (plus one non-UTC timezone run), a clean-install smoke test without dev extras, and a strict ruff lint over the whole repo. It is one of the release-engineering pieces covered in tour step 15.

sections.title: Triggers and concurrency
sections.explanation: Runs on pushes to `main` and branches named like `v1.2.3`, and on pull requests. The concurrency group keyed on `github.ref` cancels superseded runs for the same branch or PR.

sections.title: Test matrix
sections.explanation: Tests every supported Python version with `fail-fast: false` so one failure does not hide others. An extra 3.12 entry sets `TZ=America/New_York`, catching tests that only pass in UTC, which matters for a project built around point-in-time trading dates. The job name template appends the timezone when present.

sections.title: Clean-install smoke test
sections.explanation: Installs the package without dev extras and imports `tradingagents` and `cli.main`, catching runtime dependencies that were only present via dev extras (the comment cites a past python-dotenv omission).

sections.title: Strict lint
sections.explanation: Installs ruff and lints the entire repository; the comment notes the repo is fully clean under the strict selection, with generated `results/` excluded through pyproject configuration.

.github/workflows/release-assets.yml.overview: Builds the sdist and wheel from a release tag and attaches them to the GitHub release, so a version can be pip-installed straight from the release URL without cloning. It runs on published releases or manually with a tag input. Covered in tour step 15 alongside CI and the container setup.

sections.title: Purpose and triggers
sections.explanation: The header comment documents the install-from-release use case. Triggers are a published release or `workflow_dispatch` with a required `tag`, which allows attaching builds to an older release by hand.

sections.title: Permissions and concurrency
sections.explanation: Top-level `permissions: {}` grants nothing by default; the job opts into `contents: write` only. Concurrency is keyed on the tag and does not cancel in progress, so two uploads for the same tag serialize rather than abort each other.

sections.title: Job setup and checkout
sections.explanation: Resolves `TAG` from the manual input or the release event and exposes the workflow token to `gh`. Checkout uses `refs/tags/<tag>` explicitly because release branches share their tag's name, which would otherwise be ambiguous.

sections.title: Version consistency check
sections.explanation: Extracts `__version__` from `tradingagents/__init__.py` with a regex and fails if `v<version>` does not equal the tag, preventing mislabeled artifacts.

sections.title: Build, smoke-install and upload
sections.explanation: Builds with `python -m build`, installs the wheel into a fresh venv and imports from `/tmp` so modules load from the wheel rather than the checkout, also asserting that the packaged `cli/static/welcome.txt` data file is present. Finally `gh release upload --clobber` attaches the artifacts.

Dockerfile.overview: A two-stage container build for the TradingAgents CLI on `python:3.13-slim`. The builder stage installs the package into a virtualenv; the runtime stage copies that venv, runs as an unprivileged user, and uses `tradingagents` as the entrypoint. It pairs with `docker-compose.yml` in tour step 15.

sections.title: Builder stage
sections.explanation: Creates `/opt/venv`, puts it on `PATH`, copies the source and runs `pip install .` without cache. Installing into a venv makes the whole dependency set a single directory that can be copied into the slim runtime image.

sections.title: Runtime environment
sections.explanation: Starts a fresh slim image with unbuffered output (important for the live terminal UI) and sets `TRADINGAGENTS_IN_DOCKER=1`, which the comment says lets update notices name the rebuild command. The prebuilt venv is copied from the builder.

sections.title: Non-root user and entrypoint
sections.explanation: Creates `appuser` and pre-creates `~/.tradingagents` with the right ownership so a mounted volume for data is writable. The app source is copied with `--chown`, and `ENTRYPOINT ["tradingagents"]` means container arguments become CLI arguments.

docker-compose.yml.overview: Compose definitions for running the CLI in a container, optionally alongside a local Ollama server. The default service reads secrets from `.env` and persists data in a volume; the `ollama` profile adds an Ollama container and a CLI service preconfigured to use it. Covered in tour step 15.

sections.title: Main tradingagents service
sections.explanation: Builds from the local Dockerfile, loads API keys from `.env`, and mounts either `TRADINGAGENTS_DATA_DIR` or a named volume at `~/.tradingagents` so results, caches and memory persist. `tty` and `stdin_open` are required for the interactive Rich prompts.

sections.title: Ollama server (profile)
sections.explanation: Runs `ollama/ollama` with its model store on a named volume, only when the `ollama` profile is enabled.

tests/test_date_boundaries.py.overview: Verifies that yfinance OHLCV requests (get_YFin_data_online and load_ohlcv) pass an inclusive end date to the downloader so the analysis day is included.

tests/test_env_overrides.py.overview: Tests TRADINGAGENTS_* environment-variable overrides of the default config, covering string, int, bool coercion, reasoning settings, empty values, and invalid input errors.

tests/test_fred.py.overview: Tests the FRED macro vendor: alias-to-series resolution, missing-key handling, markdown report formatting, look-ahead-safe windows and vintages, router integration, and keeping the API key out of error messages.

tests/test_fundamentals_lookahead.py.overview: Tests that yfinance and Alpha Vantage fundamentals withhold live-only company profiles from historical runs while live runs still receive the full profile.

tests/test_ohlcv_date_column.py.overview: Tests OHLCV date-column normalization across yfinance versions and that cleaning a frame produces an indicator-ready copy without mutating the input.

tests/test_polymarket.py.overview: Tests the Polymarket vendor: filtering closed/past markets, ranking by volume, probability formatting, network-error resilience, and router category routing.

tests/test_statement_knowledge_time.py.overview: Tests that Yahoo and Alpha Vantage withhold financial statements and insider trades lacking filing dates from past-dated runs, and that SEC EDGAR is the default statement vendor.

tests/test_vendor_errors.py.overview: Tests the vendor error hierarchy and that the router catches base error types, falling through unconfigured or unavailable vendors correctly.

tests/test_yahoo_rate_limit.py.overview: Tests Yahoo rate-limit and outage handling across price, indicator, fundamentals and snapshot paths, distinguishing vendor unavailability from genuine absence of data.

tests/test_yahoo_snapshot.py.overview: Tests the verified market snapshot builder: excluding future rows, weekend fallback, empty-data errors, look-back caps, tool delegation, and sub-cent price precision.

tests/test_yfinance_stale_ohlcv_guard.py.overview: Tests the stale-OHLCV guard that rejects price frames whose latest row is far older than the as-of date, and its propagation through yfinance fetching and the router.

tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/ne.overview: yfinance news vendor returning ticker and global news within a look-ahead-safe window, with search fallback, coverage-gap detection and outage reporting.

tests/test_backtest.py.overview: Tests for the backtest grid runner and summary: grid construction, skipping cells already logged, settlement after the sweep, failure isolation, run-id safety, and directional hit-rate/alpha scoring.

tests/test_cli_memory_log.py.overview: Tests that the CLI run path records decisions in the memory log like propagate does, reports resume status, and writes its state log, using fake graph, live display and message buffer doubles.

tests/test_memory_log.py.overview: Extensive test suite for the trading memory log: storing and parsing decisions, deferred reflection and settlement against benchmarks, past-context injection into the portfolio manager, legacy removal, rotation, and concurrent/durable settlement.

tests/test_memory_pointintime.py.overview: Tests point-in-time gating of memory lessons so historical (backtest) runs only see reflections resolved before the run date while live runs remain unfiltered.

tests/test_rating_integrity.py.overview: Tests rating extraction integrity: labelled ratings win, argued-against or quoted ratings are not misread, refusals become REVIEW, and the signal, memory log, backtest and CLI agree on the same decision.

tests/test_report_html.py.overview: Tests the self-contained HTML report page: written unless declined, no scripts or remote fetches, escaped header values, section navigation, heading/rating, and the inert packaged logo.

tests/test_signal_processing.py.overview: unittest suite for parse_rating and extract_rating covering explicit labels, markdown variants, fullwidth colons, whole-word matching and REVIEW defaults.

tests/test_undated_tools_as_of.py.overview: Tests point-in-time behavior of undated tools (insider data, Polymarket odds, company identity, indicators) and that vendor outages are reported as unavailable rather than missing symbols or leaked dates.
